🌅 Market News Digest
[Jul 27-28, 2026 EST]

🔥 Top Stories
• Global chip selloff deepens — AI-spending fears and China competition hammer semis; KOSPI hit circuit breakers, Nikkei/Taiwan weaker, Nasdaq futures lower.
• Fed decision in focus — swaps still price a quarter-point move with dissent risk; Citadel now sees surprise hike, gold and crypto wobble.
• Middle East easing pulls oil lower — US-Iran talks and Hormuz diplomacy weigh on crude; Brent/WTI fall to multi-day lows despite lingering strike risks.
• Japan quake triggers tsunami warning — M7.1 quake near Kumamoto briefly disrupts transport and factories; TSMC/Honda/Kyushu operations affected.
• J&J to settle talc litigation for $5.5B — proposed deal covers about 76,000 ovarian cancer claims, with first payments starting in 2027.
• Nvidia scrutiny intensifies — Huang heads to DC amid $750B AI-deal frenzy, rising credit stress, and a reported Taiwan chip-smuggling probe.

⛽ Oil & Energy
• Saudi Aramco Jazan refinery hit; Libya Mellitah gas complex halted then resumes; QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure.
• Russia extends gasoline export ban as drone strikes keep refining pressured; Venezuela PDVSA shuts El Palito for maintenance.

📊 Markets & Macro
• Asia risk-off across the board — KOSPI down over 10%, Nikkei/Taiwan slide, futures weak; Europe set to open softer.
• RBA keeps hike bias alive — Bullock says inflation is still too high and more tightening may be needed; next decision remains open.
• Japan inflation stays hot — core CPI holds at 2.7%, backing the case for higher-for-longer BOJ normalization.
• Japan fiscal/bond focus — Katayama stresses market communication, no JGB buybacks, and a normal-rate environment.
• China liquidity steady — PBOC injects 305.5B yuan via 7-day repos, keeping policy rate unchanged.

🌍 Geopolitical
• US-Iran-Israel tensions remain live — Trump says talks are ongoing; Israel says it wants to hit Iran’s energy sites but is being restrained by Washington.
• Israel-Lebanon talks advance — US-backed Rome negotiations on border/security framework are slated for Aug 4-6.
• Ukraine conflict spills wider — Russia alleges Ukrainian strikes in Iraq and on Iranian shipping; senators move on Russia sanctions.

🪙 Crypto & DeFi
• Bitcoin drops under $64k — about $100M liquidated in the past hour; Ether also falls as risk appetite fades.
• Prediction markets win reprieve — Kalshi and Polymarket win a pause against Minnesota’s ban.
• Franklin Templeton backs crypto clarity — the $1.8T manager urges the US Senate to pass the Crypto Clarity Act.

🏛️ Regulatory & Policy
• Tariff risk rises — US probes Chinese factories in Vietnam, Brazil seeks WTO consultations, and USTR says new tariffs should not add fresh economic damage.
• US Senate vote watch — Clayton advances for top intelligence role; funding bill chatter builds; Zelenskiy visit raises sanctions focus.
• South Korea mulls retail leverage curbs — watchdog weighs limits after heavy losses in single-stock leveraged ETFs.

🏢 Corporate
• Nvidia/Meta double down on AI infra — Nvidia linked to massive Texas data-center lease; Meta and BlackRock unveil an El Paso campus plan.
• Big tech debt stress shows up — FT says AI capex is pushing hyperscaler bonds toward junk-like spreads.
• Strong beats from heavyweights — Nucor, Barclays, Unilever, UPS, Royal Caribbean, Centene, Coca-Cola, and Hilton mostly topped estimates.
• Consumer/industrial mixed — Mercedes guides slightly below prior-year revenue; Adobe outperforms, while Samsung, SK Hynix, and SK Telecom plunge.
• Travel/retail/outlook — Singapore Air posts a loss; Coca-Cola resumes Fairlife production after a hack; BuzzFeed rises on a 35% workforce cut plan.
